notes.title: Happy Holidays!
notes.notes:
Happy Holidays!

It's been one year since harvest Island release!!! Woooo! I'm proud to have made this game. And I'm also grateful for the fans that stuck around and enjoyed the game as well. 

Throughout the entire year, I've been updating Harvest Island and improving on where it needs best. The community has been helpful and most welcoming in sharing their opinion and their feedback in regards to the game. Most of you loved Harvest Island and a few have not. The ones that didn't liked it voiced their strong opinions about the game and they were crucial to me in fixing the game.

Since the game's release, it was buggy, lacked horror elements, and didn't have a strong premise to start with. Now, with all the updates and patches, the game has significantly improved. A lot of illustrations were added into the game, making Harvest Island more unhinged and dark. More different types of jump scares were added. An extended ending that offers more lore to the game's story. Several bug fixes since release, UI improvements, and a developer's guide that helps you navigate in the game.

Overall, Harvest Island is grim and horrifyingly darker than it once was since release. It is a must try! So, Harvest Island will be at a 40% discount this steam Autumn sale as well as the DLC!

There's so much I've learned since making Harvest Island. I've learned what it takes to make a good game and how much time it's required to make one. And from all of that experience that I've learned, my next game will be even better than Harvest Island. It's inspired by Spirited Away!

notes.title: Harvest Island goes Unhinged
notes.notes:
There's been a lot of updates since Harvest Island release and most of it has been bug fixes, new content, and added horror. Now, it's time to go even darker. So, Harvest Island will go unhinged. That means more illustrations to showcase the gore and darkness of the game. Pixel art can only do so much. But with the added illustrations, horrific scenes become much stronger and more nerve wracking. The game's sinister undertone will be elevated to a greater height.

There are new illustrations to Becky's story. This helps ground the story and build tension. You'll also see graphic images [spoiler]of kids dying as well.[/spoiler]

[spoiler][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37605883/fd768ba55955dbde5f970716d7fc1c91665674f5.png[/img][/spoiler]

There are new illustrations [spoiler]for dead animals.[/spoiler] This is horrific and gory. [spoiler] All dead animals you see will have an illustration when you interact with them.[/spoiler]  You'll probably never look at a moose the same way ever again...

[spoiler][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37605883/367abb24f9bc2294d3f8969aed482b72ceb2c320.png[/img][/spoiler]

There are new illustrations showcasing skeletons.

[spoiler]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37605883/eb1ae886091e013b3f88f9718fa6b82f8abc617a.png[/img]
[/spoiler]

More object illustrations to ground the world more. Radio, skulls, and other objects. They are dark and creepy to look at. It elevates the immersion a lot.

[spoiler]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37605883/cc53b8d82b39f560249ff9b44651e5da21f423d9.png[/img][/spoiler]

Added icons to show the day/afternoon/morning/night in the game. Also added icons to show if it's hightide/low tide. This will help the players know the current time and the current tide.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37605883/aee7922cec2ca356c4c63e116227ff1b3790737f.png[/img]

I've also added more unique jump scares. Having one type of jump scares can be predictable so sprinkling different types of jump scares will keep you on your toes.

All of these illustrations will elevate the game's horror/darkness and the game's lore. The amount of illustration in this game is over 60+. These illustrations make a huge difference in how you play and see the game.

Harvest Island is now translated to Korean! And the price is adjusted to the Korean market. It is now 13,000 Won!

I think with these new illustrations added, it'll make the game better than before.

Happy Harvest Island 1st year Anniversary,
Yobob

notes.title: Harvest Island DLC!
notes.notes:
Harvest Island is going to have a DLC! I've asked the community if they would like a "Multiple Expanded Endings" for Harvest Island and the support is great! For a small niche community, this is good support! I'm already developing this DLC. Since my last announcement of a DLC, I had to think about what content would be good for it. So I brained stormed a little bit more, reread the reviews on how to improve the game more (Within my limitations/budget) and looked at the future of Harvest Island and it's sequel/prequel.

There are only 3 things that has reoccurred within the recent reviews.
1) People expect Harvest Island to be like stardew valley but horror (which is not)
2) UI is clunky (Limitations from the game engine. Out of my power as a developer. Fixing this would take an enormous budget/time and needs to be ported to a new engine.)
3) The story's ending isn't finished. (This is something I can fix)

I think Harvest Island should have a good ending. Where there are no to be continues. I'm doing this because Harvest Island sequel/prequel is on a hold due to budget issues. And I think waiting years before I get the budget to start developing it to complete the story is too much of a wait. And by then, I think people will forget about Harvest Island. I wish I had the budget for it. I honestly do. I have such great ideas... (This is why I'm making a smaller game called A Journey's End which is more affordable.)

So, making a DLC is the 2nd best thing. And it's time to add a good ending to Harvest Island. That's why I'm making this multiple expanded ending where it'll have 4 endings in total. This is very different from the alternative endings which I am not doing. Multiple endings are endings where all the endings are a part of the lore and story to the overall game.

Samantha's Ending
Will's Ending
Father's Ending
Mother's Ending

All of these endings will tie together to end Harvest Island in one complete cohesive story. And these endings are obtained during late game.

I won't be able to develop the sequel/prequel to Harvest Island but you will experience the conclusion of Harvest Island and be once again moved by the story its told.

And the price will be $4.99 for this DLC. There will be new character portraits, illustrations, trophies/achievements, music, and a bit of gameplay! Stay tuned for the release! (I have been secretly developing this before the announcement, so it'll be released! I'm almost done!)

And to update on the current development on 'A Journey's End' If you're interested in supporting this development, follow me on youtube and wishlist the game!

notes.title: A Journey's End
notes.notes:
This will mark the end of Harvest Island V 2.0 development! I won't be doing V 2.0 Harvest Island since porting to the new engine is a massive task and requires more budget than I realize. After 3 weeks into the development in V 2.0, I needed to seek advice from other devs to see if this was the correct approach and it's not. One of the biggest advice I got was that porting requires a large fan base and you do it when you have it.

Even though V 2.0 is a great idea for the community, it's a horrible decision as of right now for me.

There's just not enough support for V 2.0 unfortunately. My fan base needs to be bigger. 

Right now, the community for Harvest Island is extremely small, very niche size. There's not much support in Harvest Island V2.0 after it's been announced. After three weeks of development, I've decided to stick with RPG Maker. And Maybe in the future, I will make a 3D version of Harvest Island instead. A remake. As of now, I'm very happy how this game turned out. It's complete.

Oh! And I added steam achievements! That's the last big update!

Harvest Island is great as it is. it tells a compelling story and succeeds in making you fall in love with the characters. The characters are very well written. There's enough horror in this game to make you feel extremely paranoid. A new experience for gamers.

There are 0 bugs in Harvest Island. I've supported every key aspect in this game and tried my utmost best to make this game as best as it could be with the given tools I have. A lot of people liked Harvest Island. Steamers who played and followers who watch their favorite streamers play, loved the story. 

I can't stress enough how great of a game this is in terms of storytelling. A lot has changed since the release and I've listened to every feedback the community has to offer and fixed the problems (With the exception of UI). Current fans are happy with how Harvest Island turned out. And I'm happy they liked the game.

I've supported Harvest Island for 4 months, and I believe it's time to move on to a new project. I will continue to keep this relationship with the community and be upfront with all of the development things I do. I thank you guys for purchasing Harvest Island and I am deeply appreciated for the community support. Along the way, If I have any ideas that'll improve Harvest Island, I'll be sure to update the game and let you know.

I will leave the price of Harvest Island to $15. I truly want people to experience this Horror farming simulator. It's a very must try experience.

And now, I present you my next game I've been developing for three weeks now. It's called, [url=https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/yobob/a-journeys-end]A Journey's End.[/url]

I am doing a[url=https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/yobob/a-journeys-end] kickstarter[/url] for this project and if you like to support this new game, please [url=https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/yobob/a-journeys-end]follow the project[/url]. Here's a sneak peak of what I'm working on.

notes.title: Harvest Island V2.0 Development
notes.notes:
Happy New Year!

Harvest Island will undergo Version 2.0. The game engine Harvest Island uses is called RPG Maker and it is extremely limited in what features I can add to the game. 

Players have voiced their problems when playing Harvest Island and it's something I'm having difficult fixing because of the current engine. It is out of my current development power.
-Bad UI
-Grid based movement
-Noi Minimap
-Non traditional farming UI
-Clunky gameplay
This is all inherent based on the engine.
(playing on the controller is a lot better)

So, I will be porting the game from RPG Maker to Godot. This will allow the game to be extremely smooth to run with added features. Like watering in a 5x5 space with a charge effect.
Features that I plan to add with this new powerful engine.
-Porting to ps5 and switch
-Overhaul UI
-Overhaul Character Movements
-Overhaul Game Mechanics
-Better performance
-Voice acting Jap & Eng
-Traditional farming UI elements and features
-More Animations/higher framed animations
-And more game mechanic features

But this will be a side project for me. So expect development time to be 1-2 years or so (Could be more). The reason is I have to remake this entire game in a new engine. And that takes serious time. I'm also going to be working on a new game, so this V 2.0 is going to really be a side project.

Harvest Island will drop in base price from $25 to $15 for Harvest Island V 1.0. Once V2.0 comes out, the price will jump back up to $25. Price take effect after the Winter Sale. So, getting the game now during the winter sale is a very great deal, especially if you want to try it. And also purchases will help fund 2.0. If more sales happen, then the development time will become shorter as I will prioritize getting V 2.0 out.

The reason I'm dropping the price is because it might be too expensive to a lot of people for this indie game. And I just want people to play the game and enjoy the storyline. I can't stress enough how great the story is.

Because the game will drop in price to $15, some of you who bought the game before the base price might be a little upset and could've waited another 3 months in buying Harvest Island. But! Your early purchased really helped the game out a lot. You guys are the sole contributors that helped Harvest Island be better than when it was first released. I was able to add a lot more content to the game because of that extra funding. I was able to add that Extended ending and commission a few more illustration for a proper ending. I was also able to add a Story B to the game to help bring more tension to the early parts of the game, and I was able to add more content, specifically more horror content to the game. And many many bug fixes as well! I sincerely thank those early contributors. Those early purchases helped elevate Harvest Island to a new level of polish.

It's very worth the game to try and to experience the main story line. And! Leave a review if you liked the game!

notes.title: Secrets of the Gods Update
notes.notes:
The gods have revealed Becky's past in Harvest Island's new update, Secrets of the gods. A story that intertwines the fate of Will and Samantha in escaping Harvest Island. Key items found in ambiguous places that helped Will and Samantha during their escape is explained in Becky's fight for survival. Along with Harvest Island's extended ending, escape one last time as the gods have granted you this final journey's climax!

There's so much to write and I'm excited to share my news to everyone!

It's been over a month since the launch of Harvest Island. I have been really busy fixing a lot of issues and for the most part, everything is polished. It's day and night to how Harvest Island was first launch vs how it is now. There's so much more horror moments that'll scare you. I have to hold my breath to make sure I wouldn't get jump scare when I tested my own game. And there were times I did get scared because I wasn't paying attention.

Harvest Island is such a unique game because I wanted to challenge the expectations of the farming sim genre. By making it a horror, it creates a lot of new opportunities in the farming sim that most developer wouldn't explore in making. I wanted to focus on the storytelling, the dark tones (Especially the scary music and the Sound effects), and the emphasis on exploration - that's where the fun in the game is at.

There has been a lot of patches since the game's release. Over 60! The feedback that you guys have shared helped Harvest Island a lot. I've read so many reviews on steam, lurking on twitch and youtube, and took the time to address every critique I've heard. I can't stress enough how important that was for this game and it really helped. The improvements are all across the board. All-around balancing, expanding existing ideas, and adding more eerie horror moments.

It truly is like day and night to how Harvest Island is now vs how it was since released. I can't even begin to describe the amount of changes the game underwent. 

And finally, the extended ending. The journey of Harvest Island was left open ended. There wasn't an ending but a cliff hanger. Now, there is a proper ending. And as you reach that ending, you'll be extremely excited to know what the game has to offer in the future. I'll let you experience that instead of me telling you!

And! Another surprising news! I've added a story B to the game! Story A is Will and Sam which is the main story but B helps add more depth to story A. This pretty much elevates the writing a lot. Sometimes the game can be a slow start and it takes a while to get to the horror, which is the meat of the game, but with story B, it immediately starts, promising you to stick around until the very end and to experience Harvest Island's gripping story.

Lastly, I've introduced another god statue in your bedroom. This god statue gives permanent bonuses to help the game progress faster! It expands on the existing idea of God Idols and emphasizes the usage of it. This helps the game's balancing tremendously because now the game can be played in two ways. An adventure game without the farming aspect (Story Mode), or a farming sim (Normal Mode) that slowly turns into an adventure game and becomes the story mode in mid game.

I encourage everyone to try/play/revisit Harvest Island because Harvest Island is unique. It combines the extreme two genres together. And with the added new content, it elevates the writing to a new level. Harvest Island tells a compelling story that will stick with you for a very long time, even after you've finished the game. It's worth the play!

Yobob

notes.title: Harvest Island Thanks Community
notes.notes:
Since the release of Harvest Island, it was pretty buggy and difficult to progress due to balancing issues. I spent the next week fixing, balancing, and listening the community's feedback. Even reading positive/negative reviews online with the harsh reviews on youtube. Now, the game is even more polished than before. I couldn't have done it without you guys.

Even though the game had a really bad start at launch, the review of 87% on steam means that I have done a satisfactory job for you guys that you can experience harvest island bug free and stress free! I'm very happy as I watch streamers play my game through twitch. Their reaction was priceless and there were a few long streams that lasted over 5+ hours! The story was pretty gripping to them! I even had a review where I changed a streamers life! Wow! I didn't think I could do that!

As my work slowly starts to die down (Finally), I will continue to fix bugs here and there when the community brings it up! There isn't much more to fix, since the game is balanced in story mode, and the normal mode is challenging enough to enjoy. Most of the work that you guys ask for QOL - These are three issues that I have heard. UI is bad, Movement/controls is bad and there's no map. These are really big issues but I cannot address these at all. It's just too difficult to implement in RPG Maker. My game engine has a big limitation. It wasn't made in unity where all of these can be fixed. Sorry guys =/ The game was designed to be a story-driven horror farming simulator. Emphasis on story telling. And judging from the reviews, I have delivered that. I'm a solo developer that had to make some tough choices when designing the game. Those are the 3 I could not overcome. But the experiences that this game provided allowed you guys to forgive these issues to a degree.

As for the future of Harvest Island. Some people might be wondering if there's a sequel. Of course there is! It ended off at a cliff hanger. A story needs to have an ending! It'll be a very long time before that sequel happens. In the meantime, I'll be working on the prequel, which was released back in 2019 as a demo. As the community builds up, and as Harvest Island continues to grow, this makes me feel like game development has been worth it. Starting out with nothing from scratch, and building upon it, I'm happy with how things turned out. As an indie developer, this has been a small success for me! Thank you guys for following me up until release, and thank you for being patient with me for fixing all these bugs when the game came out as well as giving me feedback, and reporting bug issues! I appreciate all your help!

I am a very transparent developer and this is what I need to get done before the release.
Music - I need to add more music to the game.
Polishing - The game requires a lot of balancing. This means testers needs to replay the game every time I make massive changes to the game's balancing and this can take weeks to finish. The game also requires more cut scenes and more writing. The story is complete and written. That won't change, but the extra writing is for more world building and more character development. There is also new illustrations that needs to be fitted into the game as well and that can take a week or more to import and fit for each dialogue.
Translation - This is taking the most of my time this past two months. The amount of work to translate 6 languages is insane. I'm about maybe 50% done with this. Once that's done, there's the translation testing which hasn't even started because of the sheer amount of work from importing the translations work to the game AND programing the translations to fit in the game without causing any bugs/cut offs and other little annoying bugs that international players will face. I have tested my game in english but not other languages. Also keep in mind these translators are oversees and it takes roughly 16- 24h for them to respond which adds more time to the development.

I'm sorry that I have to delay the game, but it must be done. I do not want to publish a game that's filled with bugs, lack of polish, and subpar development. I've been pulling so many all nighters to make it to the release date but it's just impossible. The translators are struggling to meet deadlines due to unforeseen circumstances, there's not enough time for testing in their languages for better quality of translations, and there's just not enough time for me to test my game which most of the development time has been towards translations and fixing translations problems.

Two months is not enough time to finish all of these big tasks. I need more time to finish a game where you can enjoy playing.

The release date will be between June - September this year.

Hi,

It's been a while but I have good news! I'm seriously starting a youtube channel to help promote Harvest Island more. This is a good thing for you because I'll be making Harvest Island Content! So, some of these content will reveal new areas in Harvest Island, but it's purely comical. Sometimes I'll post developer progress but most of the time, I just want to make you laugh. It's something I can do while developing Harvest Island at the same time since I know you guys have been waiting for this game for a long time. If you followed me in the super early stages, that's 2 years!

As for the game Harvest island. I know the biggest question is when will it be finished? Well, I have the entire game development road map planned out and I have a set date when I want to finish this game. This is pretty much what I have left to do to finish the game.

This is literally taken out of my notes from the big canvas I have written... But I'll explain more after you take a quick glance at it. (The sloppy writing is from me using a mouse lol)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37605883/6b569d2a7ed22969f0af6c95b3aaf6ea0908e01c.png[/img]

The main art which is all of the environmental art is 85-90% done.
The illustration is probably 20% done. This isn't a big deal since I have someone else working on these. So it shouldn't affect the release of the game.
Water tides is a code for me to say that, replace all the water in the game and be sure to add low tides and high tides. Pretty much a rework of the beaches in Harvest Island. This is maybe 10% finished. I still have to program a few things before the tides are final.
And then there's the secret animal map. That's pretty much is a secret :) But this is 0% done. If people have been following my dev log on my website, wild animals are really important.

Next we have Eventing. This just means to me that I have to create cutscenes for the game. Particularly the main story. And I'm talking about the ending of my game. So, you can say that the entire game's cutscenes is about 50% complete. The other 50% is the game's end game. This also implies other background programing I have to do like achievements, quests, and NPC Dialogue.

Story is 90% finished. All I have to do is write the game's lore. Which will take a while. And also write the the game's ending which is already planned out. I can't finish this without finishing the art so this will take a while for me to even start writing the game's ending. Plus there's the illustrations I have to wait on as well.

Testing. This is pretty much 0%. I have tested the game while I was developing it. So if things broke, I would fix it quickly, but small bugs that I wouldn't even think of testing would take some time for me to find them. Plus I'm going to find friends and have them play the game blindly. You can consider testing as polishing phase. Which will take a huge amount of time from me because I would be playing the game beginning to end like 100x to find bugs with different style playthroughs. And the game is pretty long and kinda open world. Would you even consider stardew valley open world? Well, you can say my game has the freedom to explore.

Easter egg island. That's just code for me to design the game's easter eggs. Yeah, it's pretty much self explanatory. If you guys played the beta, I'm sure you found game references. This island is pretty much answering those references. This is at 0% but I already have planned everything out for this.

And finally music. I'll be writing a lot of music. The game's music is probably 40%-50% done. Writing music is pretty quick for me unless I have to write a 5 min orchestral piece. We will see how my testers say about my music. If it's bad, I'm upping the level of music. If it's good, You can expect the game to release sooner. Also, I'm thinking about adding a singer which I already have lined up.

And that's pretty much everything currently with Harvest Island. So when will the game get released? I'm too afraid to give you the date because this is a lot of work, but I made deadlines for myself to finish. (Hopefully in a understandable time frame that doesn't kill me) This lets you peek into how soon Harvest Island will be finished and I hope that this is enough to keep you waiting.

notes.title: About Harvest Island
notes.notes:
[b]About the Developers[/b]


Hello everyone!

Man, the steam summer festival is kinda big, huh? Put your game on steam and bam, you cross your fingers and hope that people will play your game. Actually, in this situation, you cross your fingers and hope that you get noticed. Well, I'm optimistic. (3 years of optimism...)

It took me nearly two months to finish the demo of Harvest Island. 16h/day and lots and lots of sleepless nights. Do you know why? Because I had just finished developing Em-A-Zurvival and I got an email notification from steam with the subject heading, "STEAM SUMMER FESTIVAl!"

My thoughts were, ok. ok. Sounds cool. *Reads email more* The $%^&# I only have two weeks to get a steam page going and then two months two release a demo?!

And that was the beginning of my craziness. *Sips tea with pinky up*

Keep in mind. I'm a solo developer. That means most of the work is done by me.

As you can see, I can't think straight because I have so much work to do. Even when writing this. *Laughs crazily from stress*

So if you want to know more about me, yobob, I have a website that describes all about me and my thoughts.
https://www.yobobgames.com/our-story


[b]About the game[/b]


It's a story driven 2d top down game about Will and Samantha who explores the island just out of curiosity. The gods are pretty much watching you and you have to give bless to the statues.
Like so
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37605883/f4599484831ba3b4c3ba1797a132a08aec70617d.png[/img]

Once you give bless to the gods, they either reward you or not. They're gods so, ehhh. It's fantasy religion. They don't even need to give you anything. (Almost like real life lol...)

While you go around hunting things on the island to give to the gods, there are fun side things you can do. Like fishing.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37605883/c4fb752a08ee2c4e57bf4bb1ed3d724a65d3f8eb.png[/img]

Or milking a cow. You can pet them too.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37605883/87b4df5f3241b166cca1853265a84410be3aa7d0.png[/img]


Or the funnest of them all...picking up a twig. There's going to be lost of those because eventually you'll need to craft stuff!


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37605883/19abfafdfd970a16ff577ff122965c000204cb01.png[/img]


That's most of what I wanted to say about the story. The rest, play it and discover it. There are more "activities" than what I have told you.

So wishlist the game!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1292500/Harvest_Island/
